title: ADHD Body Doubling: What It Is + How to Do It When You Work Alone

scenes.text: Have you ever noticed that you can finally do the thing you've been avoiding for days, the second someone else is in the room? They don't help. They don't even talk. They're just there. That has a name. It's called body doubling. And if you work alone, it might be the missing piece.

visual.query: woman working on laptop at home desk

scenes.text: Body doubling means doing a task while another person is present. In person, on a video call, or even in a recorded video. The other person isn't your teacher or your boss. They're working on their own stuff. Their only job is to be there.

Why would that help? Researchers are still studying it, so nobody can promise it works for everyone. But people with A D H D describe a few things. Someone else being there turns a vague, someday task into a now task. It adds a little gentle accountability, without pressure. And it makes the hardest part, starting, feel less lonely.

visual.title: Why people say it helps
visual.note: Still being researched. Works for many, not all.

scenes.text: Here's the problem. If you're a freelancer, or you work from home, there's no office. No coworker at the next desk. Nobody notices if the proposal sits unsent for a week. So every single start depends on you alone. That's exactly where body doubling helps the most.

visual.query: woman alone at home office window

scenes.text: So where do you find a body double when you work alone? A friend on a video call, both working quietly. A coffee shop or a coworking space, where everyone around you is working. Body double with me videos on YouTube, with a timer running. Or an app that sits with you while you work.

scenes.text: Here's how to make it actually work. Step one. Pick one task, not your whole list. Step two. Make the first step tiny. Not write the proposal. Open the document. Step three. Set a timer for twenty five minutes. Step four. Start your body double, and say out loud what you're about to do. Step five. When the timer ends, you're allowed to stop. Most of the time, you won't want to.
